thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGER: spike in 5xxs + latency for inference requests in us-west-2. Error rate 12% -> 55% over the last 7m. Root route: /v1/generate -> candidate fallback routing engaged.
infra-bot: Auto-scaling attempted, 3 scale actions in last 6m. Fallback policy triggered: route_to_region=eu-west-1 for model_variant=rw-infer-7b-q4.
sara: I'm on it. Observing sudden increase in short retries from a handful of clients — looks like exponential backoff not honored.
ben: seeing high traffic to eu-west-1 now, latencies there spiking too. Could be a cascading failover loop: us-west degraded -> smart-routing sends to eu -> eu overloaded -> policy sends back -> clients retry -> thundering herd.
mica: digging through routing logs. Found policy change at 1728344940 by ops that lowered primary capacity threshold from 80% to 40% for auto-fallback. That would make fallback trigger too eagerly.
ryan: tagging @sara @ben — take primary mitigation. I'll prepare pager handoff in 20m if we need escalation.
sara: immediate mitigation idea: temporarily disable cross-region fallback for the affected model_variant and pin to local queue. Can we flip that quick via console?
ops: I can flip policy. Making a small change to routing policy: set fallback.enabled=false for model_variant=rw-infer-7b-q4 in us-west-2.
ops: done. change_id=chg_2026_1728345721. Monitoring.
ben: after flip, 5xxs in us-west are still high but eu-west intake has dropped ~62%. Host CPU in us-west nodes is at 96% on some pods. Possible hot KV cache thrash from clients retrying.
sara: let's also throttle retries at the edge. Add a rate-limit bucket for the client IPs that are producing the retries. Can infra add a temporary token bucket of 100 rps with 5 burst?
infra-bot: applying rate limit rule: rl-incident-1728345790 -> 100rps / burst 5 for prefix /v1/generate from client IDs: cid:alpha, cid:gamma. Rule applied to us-west ingress LB.
linda: CS update: two customers reported degraded interactive experience (chat latencies >8s). I'm sending a note that we're investigating and will provide ETA.
cs-rep: customer A (enterprise) is on Dedicated in us-west and sees failovers to eu, wants rollback to pinned model 7b-stable. Asked for emergency config change.
sara: confirm: are those Dedicated customers using the same global smart-routing policies? If they had pins, we shouldn't be rerouting them.
ben: they were using default routing; had not pinned variant. Ops changed default policy recently which caused eager fallback — will include dedicated customers in exclude list next.
mica: reading request traces: clients are doing fast client-side retries with no jitter. Example header traces:
```
X-Retry-Count: 3
X-Client-Retry: immediate
```
We should recommend client-side backoff update, but need server-side protection now.
ryan: next steps: 1) keep fallback disabled 2) keep rate limit rules 3) spin up additional capacity in us-west for rw-infer-7b-q4 if possible 4) notify customers and offer pin
ops: spinning up 4 additional nodes in us-west reserved pool. ETA ~4m.
infra-bot: nodes provisioning started (nodepool:dedicated-usw-2). Expected ready 220s.
ben: traffic patterns show a particular customer CID 'alpha' is responsible for ~48% of retries. Can we temporarily throttle that CID harder?
sara: yes - escalate CID alpha to hard throttle 20rps. Make a per-customer circuit breaker if >50% 5xx in 2m.
ops: adding circuit-breaker rule cb-alpha-1728345875 -> 20rps. Applied. Will log and return 429 when exceeded.
linda: CS: told customer A we will offer pin to 7b-stable and separate Dedicated routing if they want; they asked to wait until we stabilize.
mica: after CB applied, request rate from alpha dropped 85%, 5xxs reduced to 9% overall. Latency still 600-1200ms higher than baseline for interactive flows.
ben: eu-west latencies normalizing now. Seems like the cascade was amplified by aggressive retry logic + policy change.
sara: root cause summary in progress: policy change reduced fallback threshold + clients with aggressive retries -> failover amplification and a thundering herd to eu-west -> overloaded eu-west attempts fall back / conflicted routing -> oscillation.
IncidentBot: Incident severity escalated to P1 (ongoing customer impact). Paging next oncall in 18m: @ryan.
ryan: I'll take full handoff at :30. If we cannot get latency back to baseline in 30m we escalate to infra-leads and request emergency capacity from cloud.
ops: capacity added is healthy, new nodes joined, warming KV caches. Seeing tail latency decline slowly.
ben: recommend follow-up config: revert the change that lowered fallback threshold and add a canary window for any future routing policy rollouts. Also add a guard: require min grace period of 5m before fallback re-enabled after a scale event.
sara: Agreed. Also propose server-side client_retry_suppression: when fallback triggers we globally apply short client-suppression header instructing SDKs to backoff for x seconds. Need SDK/contract change though.
mica: log snippet that shows the loop (simplified):
```
us-west: 503 -> client retries immediate -> smart-routing sends to eu-west
eu-west: 200/503 mixed -> eu overloaded -> smart-routing policy triggers fallback back to us-west
client: sees 503 again -> retries -> repeat
```
ops: putting a short-term automated cooldown: do not trigger region fallback more than once per 10m for same request fingerprint. Enabled change cdn_cooldown=600.
infra-bot: cooldown flag enabled in runtime routing: cdn_cooldown=600s.
linda: CS informed customers A/B/C with current mitigations and ETA 30m for full normalization. They thanked on the update but want postmortem.
ryan: prepping handoff notes for next oncall: we'll leave fallback disabled, keep cb-alpha enabled, retention of logs for 48h, start postmortem draft.
sara: I'm going offline after the handoff. Ben/Mica continue metric watch and collect sample traces for postmortem. Leave everything in
